segments: That white line behind a plane? It's not smoke.
It's a cloud the plane makes by itself.
The engines burn fuel and spit out hot water vapor.
Way up high, the air is colder than minus thirty.
The vapor hits that cold and freezes into ice crystals.
Specks of soot give the ice something to cling to.
In dry air, it's gone in seconds.
In humid air? It can last for hours.
A long trail means the air up there is damp.
So that white line? Not smoke. A cloud.
